- crypto-privacy-reviewer: Cryptography and privacy expert that reviews code, validates assumptions, and generates test cases. NOT prefixed with gsd- so it survives GSD updates. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- design-an-interface: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- git-guardrails-claude-code: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- gsd-dev-preferences: Load developer preferences into this session
- migrate-to-shoehorn: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.
- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the Obsidian vault with wikilinks and index notes. Use when user wants to find, create, or organize notes in Obsidian.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- qa: Interactive QA session where user reports bugs or issues conversationally, and the agent files GitHub issues. Explores the codebase in the background for context and domain language. Use when user wants to report bugs, do QA, file issues conversationally, or mentions "QA session".
- request-refactor-plan: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits via user interview, then file it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to plan a refactor, create a refactoring RFC, or break a refactor into safe incremental steps.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- scaffold-exercises: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.
- setup-pre-commit: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- crypto-privacy-review: Review code for cryptographic security, generate test cases and edge cases
- resolve-pr-reviews: Resolve PR Review Comments
- ship: Ship
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
=== #812 ===
engine/core: encode-side fail-closed guards for the child read-path rejects
## Context

PR #811 (issue #802) added four decode/verify-side hard rejects on the child read path whose matching produce paths do not exist yet. Per the AGENTS.md encode/decode fail-closed symmetry rule, each producer must land with a release-active `Err` guard (never `debug_assert!`) plus a test that fires in a release build — otherwise a release build can publish bytes its own decoder rejects.

## Debts

When the content-bearing write / child-publish paths land, each of these decode-side rejects needs its encode-side twin:

1. **Grant section on a child envelope** — child adoption rejects any envelope carrying a `grantSection` key (`has_grant_section`, `crates/core/src/seal/envelope.rs`). Child envelope sealing must refuse to attach one.
2. **Kind transplant** — `read_content` rejects when the sealed body kind disagrees with the parent's `ChildRef.kind` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs`). Child-ref authoring must enforce the match.
3. **Version size vs manifest size** — `content::open_content` rejects `manifest.size != version.size` (`crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs`). Today `Version::new` and DAG `assemble` take `size` independently; seal/publish must tie them.
4. **Child-ref `ipnsName` well-formedness** — the read path parses the bytes fail-closed as a canonical base36 IPNS name (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs`); child-ref authoring must emit exactly that form.

## Dependency

Depends on the engine content-bearing write / upload slice (surfaces via #807); blocks none. Related precedent: #794.

Found by the /crypto-privacy-review gate on #811.

web: scaffold apps/web toolchain and the single EngineProvider
## Goal
`apps/web` gains routing + providers + one `EngineProvider` owning the single `EngineClient`; placeholder Login + Files render. First cut of the v2 web shell — no data flow yet.

## Harvest / create
- `main.tsx` provider tree, `App.tsx` routes `/` and `/files/:nodeId?`.
- `providers/EngineProvider.tsx` owning the single `EngineClient`.
- Port `polyfills.ts` + vite buffer/wasm-worker config.

## Rewire
Placeholder Login + Files pages render behind the router; no snapshot or facade wiring yet.

## Engine seams
None wired this phase — `EngineProvider` only constructs/owns the client.

## Deps to add
`react-router-dom`, `@web3auth/mpc-core-kit`, `@toruslabs/tss-dkls-lib`, `wagmi`, `viem`, `@tanstack/react-query`.

## Tests
Web unit: provider mounts, routes resolve, build produces the wasm worker bundle.

## Gate
web unit / typecheck / build.

## Depends on
None.

Part of #642


=== #752 ===
engine: assemble the facade cold-start identity derivation and live-session wiring
Umbrella for completing the facade **cold-start sequence** — deriving the session identity and key material at login and assembling the live session behind the `Engine::start` surface.

## Context

`Engine::start` is currently the frozen facade skeleton (#623 scaffolded it; `lib.rs` / `facade.rs` note that "the full cold-start sequence … lands with the pipeline slices"). It authenticates and wires background work, but it does **not** yet derive the session identity/key material or assemble the live-session data paths. #739 (Closes #697) wired the liveness re-PUT loop into `start` but had to defer every piece that needs derived session key material or the live resolve path — see the dependent issues below.

## Scope

The cold-start sequence, end to end:

- Challenge-signature login → Web3Auth key derivation (per the auth pillar; #624 landed identity auth + refresh rotation).
- Session key material: per-scope read/write keys, per-name `Ed25519Signer`s, writer pseudonym signers — the seeded per-scope derivation with key-regression epochs.
- Live-session wiring: the resolve path, the held-record set, liveness-loop composition, and rehydrate-on-boot.
- Determinism preserved: entropy/time enter via seam traits, never a direct clock/RNG.

## Dependencies

**Depends on (upstream):**

- #624 — identity auth, refresh rotation, ops baseline (merged).
- #623 — facade scaffold + frozen `Engine::start` surface (merged).

**Blocks (dependent issues — must be built as part of / after this):**

- #750 — compose `eol_republish` sub-EOL seq+1 renewal into the cold-start liveness loop (needs the per-name `Ed25519Signer`s this issue derives).
- #751 — populate the liveness held-record set from the live resolve path (needs the live-session resolve wiring this issue assembles).

## Notes

- Referenced by #697 / #739 as "the deferred facade skeleton."
- Consumed downstream by the web shell (#642, #643) and desktop login (#650), which drive the facade.

Part of the v2 build (`v2-build`), tracked in #655.


---

### Remaining work (after #789 landed #748/#751/#750): the live-session resolve-tick driver

#789 landed the facade reads/command/events (#748), the held-record population logic (#751), and the EOL-renewal pass (#750) — all test-proven but **dormant** until a production driver populates the held set. This umbrella stays open for that live-session wiring:

- **Spawn the production resolve-tick loop** (focus-window polling) that calls `resolve_and_hold` so the held set is populated from live resolves in `start()`.
- **API base-URL config**: the loop's `ApiClient` is currently built with an empty base URL (harmless while dormant). Wire the real API base (part of the auth/config surface, still `Unimplemented`) so EOL republication actually publishes.
- **Write-seed plumbing**: `resolve_and_hold` needs the unsealed `write_scope_seed` in `HeldMaterial`, but the `Adopted` resolve outcome does not yet carry it — thread it through the resolve/gate path.

=== #802 ===
engine: project a facade snapshot and download read surface for the web client
CLOSED
## Goal
Close the facade read-surface gap that blocks the whole web browser. Today `Engine` is command-in / event-out only and `SnapshotUpdated` is a payload-free ping — the v1 UI harvest can render nothing until a key-free read surface lands. This is the natural successor to #789.

## Harvest / create
- `Engine::snapshot(folder) -> SnapshotView` projected from `sync/model::Snapshot`, **key-free**: root id; focused folder direct-children `{id,name,kind,size?,mtime?,pending,deadLetter,contentVersion}`; ancestor chain to root for breadcrumbs; current `Staleness`.
- `Engine::read_content(node) -> Bytes`.
- Per-node `pending`/`deadLetter` + an `OpProgress{opId,node,phase,error?}` channel for upload/download rows.

## Rewire
- `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` — expose `snapshot` / `download`.
- `packages/client` — `worker/protocol.ts`, `worker/commandCodec.ts`, `transport.ts`, `broadcastTransport.ts`, `facade.ts` read paths.

## Engine seams
`snapshot`, `read_content`/`download`, `OpProgress` channel.

## Tests
Rust projection unit tests + `packages/client` browser conformance over both transports (direct + broadcast).

## Gate
`cargo test` + `packages/client` browser suite.

## Depends on
None.

Part of #642

web: wire folder create, rename, move, and delete to facade commands
OPEN
## Goal
Harvest the v1 folder-mutation dialogs and wire them to facade commands.

## Harvest / create
Harvest from branch `v1`:
- `components/file-browser/{CreateFolderDialog,RenameDialog,MoveDialog,ConfirmDialog,ContextMenu,SelectionActionBar}.tsx`
- `useContextMenu`, `useFileBrowserActions.ts`
- `components/ui/{Modal,Portal}.tsx`
- `styles/{dialogs,modal,context-menu}.css`

## Rewire
- Handlers -> `facade.create` / `facade.rename` / `facade.relink` / `facade.delete`.
- `MoveDialog` picker lazily `setFocus`/`snapshot` per candidate parent — no cached tree (direct-children-only per #789).
- Pending overlay + dead-letter render from `SnapshotView`.

## Engine seams
`create`, `rename`, `relink`, `delete`, snapshot pending flags, `deadLetter` event.

## Tests
Each dialog dispatches the right command; a pending node renders; dead-letter surfaces a persistent notice.

## Gate
web unit.

## Depends on
#805.

web: wire file upload, download, and static preview through the facade

## Goal
Harvest the v1 upload + preview UI and route content through the facade.

## Harvest / create
Harvest from branch `v1`:
- `components/file-browser/{UploadZone,UploadListItem,DetailsDialog,ImagePreviewDialog,PdfPreviewDialog,TextEditorDialog}.tsx`
- `details/*` (current version only)
- `useDropUpload` (rewritten)

- Per-file progress from the op-progress channel.
- Download/preview via `facade.download` -> object-URL a Blob.

`create`/`updateContent`, `download`, op-progress.

## Tests

#802, #805.

So the honest dependency picture for #812:

- #812 → (unfiled engine content-write slice) → #807

That's a real hole in the tracker chain, not just a sequencing question. Recommend filing the engine content-bearing write/upload slice now with edges to #807 and #812, so it doesn't get discovered at #807 time. Want me to file it?

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/myankelev/.claude/skills/wayfinder

A loose idea has arrived — too big for one agent session, and wrapped in fog: the way from here to the **destination** isn't visible yet. Wayfinding is about finding that way, not charging at the destination. This skill charts the way as a **shared map** on the repo's issue tracker, then works its **decision tickets** — questions whose resolution is a decision, not slices of a build to execute — one at a time until the route is clear.

The destination varies per effort, and naming it is the first act of charting — it shapes every ticket. It might be a spec to hand off and iterate on, a decision to lock before planning starts, or a change made in place like a data-structure migration. The map is domain-agnostic — engineering work, course content, whatever fits the shape.

## Plan, don't do

Wayfinder is **planning** by default: each ticket resolves a decision, and the map is done when the way is clear — nothing left to decide before someone goes and does the thing. The pull to just do the work is usually the signal you've reached the edge of the map and it's time to hand off. An effort can override this in its **Notes** — carrying execution into the map itself — but absent that, produce decisions, not deliverables.

## Refer by name

Every map and ticket is an issue, so it has a **name** — its title. In everything the human reads — narration, the map's Decisions-so-far — refer to it by that name, never by a bare id, number, or slug. A wall of `#42, #43, #44` is illegible; names read at a glance. The id and URL don't vanish — a name wraps its link — but they ride *inside* the name, never stand in for it.

## The Map

The map is a single issue on this repo's issue tracker, labelled `wayfinder:map` — the canonical artifact. Its tickets are child issues of the map.

The map is an **index**, not a store. It lists the decisions made and points at the tickets that hold their detail; a decision lives in exactly one place — its ticket — so the map never restates it, only gists it and links.

**Where the map, its child tickets, blocking, and frontier queries physically live is tracker-specific.** The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not. Consult the tracker doc's "Wayfinding operations" section for how _this_ repo expresses them. If no tracker has been provided, default to the local-markdown tracker.

### The map body

The whole map at low resolution, loaded once per session. Open tickets are **not** listed — they are open child issues, found by query.

```markdown
## Destination

<what reaching the end of this map looks like — the spec, decision, or change this effort is finding its way to. One or two lines; every session orients to it before choosing a ticket.>

## Notes

<domain; skills every session should consult; standing preferences for this effort>

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index — one line per closed ticket: enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->

- [<closed ticket title>](link) — <one-line gist of the answer>

## Not yet specified

<!-- see "Fog of war": in-scope fog you can't ticket yet; graduates as the frontier advances -->

## Out of scope

<!-- see "Out of scope": work ruled beyond the destination; closed, never graduates -->
```

### Tickets

Each ticket is a **child issue** of the map; the tracker's issue id is its identity. Its body is the question, sized to one 100K token agent session:

```markdown
## Question

<the decision or investigation this ticket resolves>
```

Each ticket carries a `wayfinder:<type>` label — one of `research`, `prototype`, `grilling`, `task` (see [Ticket Types](#ticket-types)).

A session **claims** a ticket by assigning it to the dev driving the map, **first**, before any work, so concurrent sessions skip it. That assignee _is_ the claim: an open, unassigned ticket is unclaimed.

Blocking uses the tracker's **native** dependency relationship — essential because it renders the frontier _visually_ in the tracker's own UI, so the human sees what's takeable without opening the map. Only a tracker that lacks native blocking falls back to a body convention. A ticket is **unblocked** when every ticket blocking it is closed; the **frontier** is the open, unblocked, unclaimed children — the edge of the known.

The answer isn't part of the body — it's recorded on resolution (see [Work through the map](#work-through-the-map)). Assets created while resolving a ticket are linked from the issue, not pasted in.

## Ticket Types

Every ticket is either **HITL** — human in the loop, worked *with* a human who speaks for themselves — or **AFK**, driven by the agent alone. A HITL ticket only resolves through that live exchange; the agent never stands in for the human's side of it (a grilling agent that answers its own questions has broken this).

- **Research** (AFK): Reading documentation, third-party APIs, or local resources like knowledge bases to surface a fact a decision waits on. Resolved by a `/research` **subagent**. Use when knowledge outside the current working directory is required.
- **Prototype** (HITL): Raise the fidelity of the discussion by making a cheap, rough, concrete artifact to react to — an outline, a rough take, a stub, or UI/logic code via the /prototype skill. Links the prototype as an asset. Use when "how should it look" or "how should it behave" is the key question.
- **Grilling** (HITL): Conversation via the /grilling and /domain-modeling skills, one question at a time. The default case.
- **Task** (HITL or AFK): Manual work that must happen before a *decision* can be made — nothing to decide, prototype, or research, but the discussion is blocked until it's done. Signing up for a service so its API can be judged, provisioning access, moving data so its shape can be seen. This is the one type that *does* rather than decides — and it earns its place by unblocking a decision, not by delivering the destination. The agent drives it alone where it can (AFK); otherwise it hands the human a precise checklist (HITL). Resolved when the work is done; the answer records what was done and any resulting facts (credentials location, new URLs, row counts) later tickets depend on.

## Fog of war

The map is _deliberately_ incomplete: don't chart what you can't yet see. Beyond the live tickets lies the **fog of war** — the dim view of decisions and investigations you can tell are coming but can't yet pin down, because they hang on questions still open. Resolving a ticket clears the fog ahead of it, graduating whatever's now specifiable into fresh tickets — one at a time, until the way to the destination is clear and no tickets remain.

The map's **Not yet specified** section is where that dim view is written down: the suspected question, the area to revisit later. It's the undiscovered frontier _toward_ the destination — everything here is in scope, just not sharp enough to ticket. Write as loosely or as fully as the view allows; it doubles as a signpost for collaborators reading where the effort is headed.

**Fog or ticket?** The test is whether you can state the question precisely now — _not_ whether you can answer it now.

- **Ticket when** the question is already sharp — even if it's blocked and you can't act on it yet.
- **Not yet specified when** you can't yet phrase it that sharply. Don't pre-slice the fog into ticket-sized pieces: it's coarser than a ticket, and one patch may graduate into several tickets, or none, once the frontier reaches it.

**Not yet specified** excludes what's already decided (Decisions so far), what's already a live ticket, and what's out of scope (the next section).

## Out of scope

Fog only ever gathers _toward_ the destination. The destination fixes the scope, so work beyond it is **out of scope** — it isn't fog, and it doesn't belong in **Not yet specified**. It gets its own **Out of scope** section on the map: work you've consciously ruled out of _this_ effort. Scope, not sharpness, lands it here.

Out-of-scope work never graduates — the frontier stops at the destination — so it returns only if the destination is redrawn, and then as a fresh effort, not a resumption.

Ruling something out of scope is a scoping act, not a step on the route. When a ticket that already exists turns out to sit past the destination — mis-scoped in while charting, or exposed by a resolution — **close it** (a closed ticket is unambiguously off the frontier) and leave one line in the **Out of scope** section: the gist plus why it's out of scope, linking the closed ticket. It stays out of **Decisions so far**, which records the route actually walked — a scope boundary isn't a step on it.

## Invocation

Two modes. Either way, **never resolve more than one ticket per session** — with the exception of research tickets.

### Chart the map

User invokes with a loose idea.

1. **Name the destination.** Run a `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` session to pin down what this map is finding its way to — the spec, decision, or change. The destination fixes the scope, so it's settled first.
2. **Map the frontier.** Grill again, **breadth-first** this time: fan out across the whole space rather than deep on any one thread, surfacing the open decisions and the first steps takeable now. **If this surfaces no fog** — the way to the destination is already clear, the whole journey small enough for one session — you don't need a map. Stop and ask the user how they'd like to proceed.
3. **Create the map** (label `wayfinder:map`): Destination and Notes filled in, Decisions-so-far empty, the fog sketched into **Not yet specified**.
4. **Create the tickets you can specify now** as child issues of the map — then wire blocking edges in a **second pass** (issues need ids before they can reference each other). Wiring sorts them into the frontier and the blocked; everything you can't yet specify stays in the fog — the **Not yet specified** section.
5. **Fire the research subagents.** For each `research` ticket you just created, spin up a `/research` subagent to resolve it in parallel, capturing its findings on a throwaway `research/<name>` branch with a context pointer from the ticket.
6. Stop — charting is one session's work; it hand-resolves nothing.

### Work through the map

User invokes with a map (URL or number). A ticket is **optional** — without one, you pick the next decision, not the user.

1. Load the **map** — the low-res view, not every ticket body.
2. Choose the ticket. If the user named one, use it. Otherwise take the first frontier ticket in order. **Claim it**: assign it to yourself before any work.
3. Resolve it — **zoom as needed**: fetch the full body of any related or closed ticket on demand; invoke the skills the `## Notes` block names. If in doubt, use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`.
4. Record the resolution: post the answer as a **resolution comment**, **close** the issue, and **append a context pointer** to the map's Decisions-so-far.
5. Add newly-surfaced tickets (create-then-wire); graduate any fog the answer has made specifiable, clearing each graduated patch from **Not yet specified** so it lives only as its new ticket. If the answer reveals a ticket — this one or another — sits beyond the destination, **rule it out of scope** rather than resolving it on the route. If the decision invalidates other parts of the map, update or delete those tickets.

The user may run unblocked tickets in parallel, so expect other sessions to be editing the tracker concurrently.

2	
3	Issues and PRDs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.
4	
5	## Conventions
6	
7	- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
8	- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
9	- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10	- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
11	- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
12	- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`
13	
14	Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.
15	
16	## Pull requests as a triage surface
17	
18	**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_
19	
20	When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:
21	
22	- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
23	- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
24	- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.
25	
26	GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.
27	
28	## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"
29	
30	Create a GitHub issue.
31	
32	## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"
33	
34	Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.
35	
36	## Wayfinding operations
37	
38	Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.
39	
40	- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
41	- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
42	- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only — the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
43	- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
44	- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` — the session's first write.
45	- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and PRDs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` — `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either — resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** — the canonical, UI-visible representation. # The engine content-bearing write slice — recon report

## 0. Headline

The gap is **much bigger than "seal the bytes"**. The content plane's write half is fully built as a *library* and completely orphaned. But underneath it, **the engine has no production record-authoring or record-publishing-of-a-mutation path at all**: `seal_read_body` / `encode_envelope` appear in `crates/engine/src` **only inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules** (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2713-2879`, `:3311-3318`; `crates/engine/src/net/adopter.rs:346-532` — both under `#[cfg(test)]` at `facade.rs:1613` and `adopter.rs:337`). No production code in the engine ever authors an envelope, uploads a block, or drains the op queue.

So "Create{content: Some}" is blocked on a stack of four missing layers, only one of which is content-specific.

---

## 1. What exists already

### 1.1 `crates/engine/src/content/` — write side complete, orphaned; read side complete, wired

Zero `todo!()`/`unimplemented!()` in the directory. The asymmetry is **wiring**, not stubbing.

| Item | Location | Direction | Wired? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seal_content(plaintext, key, entropy, profile) -> Result<SealedContent, SealError>` | `content/mod.rs:86-99` | **write** | **no caller** |
| `SealedContent { content_cid, root_block, leaves }` | `content/mod.rs:48-56` | write | — |
| `ContentKey::generate(&mut impl Entropy)`, `ZeroizeOnDrop` | `content/chunk.rs:23-47` | write | — |
| `frame_and_seal(plaintext, key, entropy, profile) -> Vec<SealedChunk>` | `content/chunk.rs:78-98` | **write** (framing = `plaintext.chunks(profile.chunk_size())`, `:87`; empty → one empty leaf `:84-86`; fresh 24-byte nonce per chunk from the entropy seam `:91-92`) | test-only |
| `dag::assemble(leaves, plaintext_len, profile) -> Result<ContentDag, DagError>` | `content/dag.rs:106-137` | **write** | test-only |
| `dag::decode_root(root_block) -> RootManifest` | `content/dag.rs:159-199` | read | wired |
| `open_content(gateway, http, version) -> Result<Vec<u8>, OpenError>` | `content/mod.rs:130-177` | **read** | wired from `facade.rs:1512` |
| `read_block(gateway, http, cid_str, expected_cid, plane)` | `content/read.rs:175` | read | wired |
| `leaf_range_for_byte_range(...)` (ranged-read map) | `content/read.rs:282-305` | read | **no caller** |
| `PinMode { Hosted, External, Dual }`, `ByoIpfsConfig`, `test_connection`, `validate_endpoint` | `content/provider.rs:25-160` | placement | **no consumer anywhere** |
| `pre_flight_quota_check`, `plan_prune`, `PrunePlan` | `content/retention.rs:32-84` | policy | **no caller** |
| `ContentProfile::{PRODUCTION (1 MiB), CI (16)}`, private `chunk_size`, no `Default` | `content/profile.rs:14-59` | policy | used only by write side |
| `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES = 4 MiB` (crate-private) | `content/limits.rs:17` | both | wired |

DAG root shape (`dag.rs:79-81, 120-124`): det-CBOR `{ "chunkSize": u64, "size": u64, "links": [bytes…] }`, flat single-level, codec `DAG_ROOT_CODEC = 0x71` (`dag.rs:31`). Fan-out is an explicit open edge (`dag.rs:12-16`). Leaf/root count invariant is shared by both directions via `expected_leaf_count` (`dag.rs:207-213`, called at `:111` and `:188`).

`Version` lives in core, not engine: `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs:139-150` — `{ content_cid: Vec<u8>, content_key: SecretBytes (private, zeroizing), size: u64, modified_at: u64, unknown }`; ctor `Version::new` at `body.rs:156-169`; `content_key()` accessor `body.rs:172`; `Debug` redacts (`body.rs:205-215`).

### 1.2 `crates/core/src/content/` — the WRITE API is complete and KAT-frozen

```rust
// crates/core/src/content/seal.rs:31
pub fn seal_chunk(key: &[u8; KEY_LEN], nonce: &[u8; NONCE_LEN], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>
// crates/core/src/content/cid.rs:70
pub fn compute_cid(codec: u8, bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>
// crates/core/src/content/cid.rs:141
pub fn encode_content_cid_str(cid: &[u8]) -> String
// read side:
// seal.rs:45  pub fn open_chunk(key, sealed) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError>
// cid.rs:92   pub fn verify_cid(claimed_cid, bytes) -> Result<(), CodecError>
// cid.rs:157  pub fn decode_content_cid_str(s) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError>
```

- **"Caller-framed"** = core takes a byte slice with no index/offset/count and no size-dependent behaviour; boundaries are decided at `content/chunk.rs:84-88`. Documented consequence (`seal.rs:14-17`): a sealed chunk carries **no index or order binding**; ordering lives in the manifest `links` array and is anchored transitively through `Version.contentCid` inside the sealed metadata read-body.
- **AAD for content chunks is empty** (`seal.rs:34`, `:54`). Nonce is caller-injected, never derived; the uniqueness obligation is explicit at `seal.rs:25-28`.
- **Content keys are a stated KDF non-edge** — `crates/core/src/kdf/mod.rs:18-20` names "content keys (random per version)" as a non-edge. Minted from raw entropy at `chunk.rs:31-35`.
- Frozen constants: `CONTENT_CID_CODEC = 0x55` (`cid.rs:42`), `CONTENT_CID_MULTIHASH = 0x1e` (`cid.rs:46`), `CONTENT_CID_LEN = 36` (`cid.rs:56`).
- **Write direction is KAT-frozen**: `crates/core/kat/vectors/content/{seal,seal_reject,cid,cid_reject,cid_str_accept,cid_str_reject}.json`, pinned at `crates/core/kat/manifest.json:394-431`; encode-side byte-for-byte assertions at `crates/core/tests/kat_manifest.rs:3775-3781` and `:3872-3884`. Property test `crates/core/tests/seal_props.rs:203-224` runs on wasm32 too.
- Existing encode-side release-active guards: `cid.rs:73-76` and `cid.rs:142-145` (`assert!`, not `debug_assert!`); `dag.rs:111-115` and `dag.rs:125-131` (release-active `Err`). **Gap noted:** there is no frozen KAT for the *engine-side* DAG root block — only inline round-trip tests in `dag.rs:263-407`. `crates/engine/tests/` has no content-plane test file.

### 1.3 The read surface landed by #811 / #802

- `pub async fn snapshot(&self, folder: NodeId) -> Result<SnapshotView, EngineError>` — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1308`. One `pending_ops()` read (`:1312`) feeds both overlay and pending flags; `apply_overlay` (`:1313`); children → `SnapshotChild` with `pending`/`dead_letter`/`content_version` (`:1324-1337`); staleness classified at read time (`:1350-1357`).
- `pub async fn read_content(&self, node: NodeId) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EngineError>` — `facade.rs:1376`, inner at `:1404-1519`. Flow: base-snapshot lookup of `(kind, ipns_name)` (`:1408-1412`); pending-op-targets-it → `ContentUnavailable("content not yet published")` (`:1413-1427`); canonical base36 IPNS name parse fail-closed → `TrustViolation` (`:1434-1441`); `ChildAdopter` + `resolve` (`:1456-1473`); `Current`/`NoUpdate` → `open_at_floor` re-open (`:1477-1496`); **body-kind cross-check** vs `ChildRef.kind` → `TrustViolation` (`:1498-1504`); empty `versions` → `ContentUnavailable` (`:1506-1510`); `open_content` (`:1512-1517`) → DAG root CID verify → `manifest.size == version.size` cross-check → per-leaf CID verify + unseal → final length check. Then `project_child_version` folds size/mtime into the base snapshot (`facade.rs:1386-1388`, `sync/project.rs:50-63`).
- `OpPhase { DownloadStarted, DownloadCompleted, DownloadFailed }` — `facade.rs:438-445`; `emit_op_progress` hardcodes `op_id: None` (`facade.rs:1524`).

### 1.4 Sync / op-queue — the metadata path, and where it stops

`Command` enum verbatim at `facade.rs:235-350`; content-bearing variants at `:238-247` (`Create { …, content: Option<PlaintextContent> }`) and `:270-275` (`UpdateContent { node, content: PlaintextContent }`). `Debug` is redacting (`facade.rs:376-380`, `:77`).

`Unimplemented` return sites — error type `EngineError::Unimplemented { command: &'static str }` (`facade.rs:477-481`):
- `facade.rs:1247-1251` — `if content.is_some() { return Err(Unimplemented) }` inside the `Create` arm.
- `facade.rs:1285-1287` — the catch-all arm, which is where `UpdateContent` falls.

Test assertions: `crates/engine/tests/facade.rs:31-96` (the list), `:137-153` (`unimplemented_commands_return_their_typed_error`). Inline mirrors: `facade.rs:1984-1997`, `:2077-2089`.

The op model — `crates/engine/src/sync/op.rs:19-83`:

```rust
pub struct Op { pub target: NodeId, pub base_sequence: u64, pub kind: OpKind }   // :19-30
pub enum OpKind {
    Create { parent: NodeId, name: String, kind: NodeKind, content_staging_key: Option<Vec<u8>> }, // :37-47
    Delete { target_sequence: u64 },                                                               // :50-53
    Rename { new_name: String },                                                                   // :55-58
    Relink { from_parent: NodeId, new_parent: NodeId, cross_scope: bool, exits_granted_source: bool }, // :65-77
    UpdateContent { content_staging_key: Vec<u8> },                                                // :79-82
}
```

**The content seam already exists in the op model.** No bytes and no CIDs ride an op by design (`op.rs:11-13`); two variants carry an opaque `content_staging_key` into the `StagingStore`. `Op::update_content` (`op.rs:149`) exists with **no `src/` caller**.

Metadata command trace: `Engine::command` (`facade.rs:1232`) is the **only** write entry point — there is no public `apply`/`enqueue`/`commit`/`publish`. `Create{None}` `:1238-1256` → `mint_node_id` (`:1570`) + `base_sequence_for` (`:1563`) → `Op::create(…, None)` → `stage_and_notify` (`facade.rs:1581-1597`) → `stage_op(store, profile, op, None)` (`sync/staging.rs:47`) → `Event::SnapshotUpdated`. `Delete` `:1257-1262`, `Rename` `:1263-1267`, `Relink` `:1268-1277` are identical in shape.

**What drives publish after a metadata op: nothing.** Verified:
- `sync::rebase::replay` (`sync/rebase.rs:138`) has **no `src/` caller** — only `crates/engine/tests/sync.rs:227,271`.
- `net::publish::publish` (`net/publish.rs:115`) has exactly two callers, both liveness/repair: `net/liveness.rs:28` and `net/revival.rs:15`.
- `sync/tick.rs::run_tick_loop` (`tick.rs:178`) has **no `src/` caller**; `start` spawns `spawn_liveness_loop` (`facade.rs:1060`) and `spawn_resolve_tick_loop` (`facade.rs:1108`), both read-only. The resolve tick repaints the base cell (`:1185-1189`) and never drains the queue.
- Queue entries are removed only by the cold-start undecodable-op sweep (`facade.rs:1013-1028`).

So today a `mkdir` is durable-and-optimistic only: nothing is sealed, nothing published, and the op stays queued forever.

Rebase machinery (built, unwired): `decode_queue` (`rebase.rs:122`), `replay` (`:138`), `rebase_one` (`:193`), `OpResolution`/`DropReason`/`DeadLetterReason` (`:37-83`), add/add auto-suffix with `MAX_SUFFIX_PROBE = 10_000` (`:33`, `:217-244`), conditional delete (`:247-259`), dest-first move with `MoveRaceLost` compensation (`:291`), `rebase_update_content` resurrects a concurrently-deleted target (`:328-362`), observed repair (`:406`, `:434`), `reconcile_head` (`:445`, `:480`).

Staging: `stage_op(store, profile, op, upload: Option<&[u8]>)` — `sync/staging.rs:47-83`. `(Some(key), Some(bytes))` → budget check vs `staged_bytes_total()` then `put_staged_bytes` **before** `enqueue_op` (`:54-70`); `(Some(_), None)` → fail-closed `SeamError` (`:74-76`). `StageOutcome::RejectedOverBudget { staged, incoming, budget }` (`:17-33`). `orphan_staging_keys` GC (`:88-111`). **Critically, `staging.rs:40-42`: "no plaintext user content ever lands in the staging store at rest"** — sealing must happen in `Engine::command` before `stage_op`.

`StagingStore` seam is two planes in one trait (`seams/staging_store.rs:24-51`): FIFO op queue (`enqueue_op`/`queued_ops`/`remove_op`) + keyed sealed-bytes blob store (`put_staged_bytes`/`staged_bytes`/`remove_staged_bytes`/`staged_keys`/`staged_bytes_total`).

### 1.5 Upload / pin / quota / registry

**Engine API client (`crates/engine/src/api/client.rs`) — all four exist and are live:**

| Method | Route | line |
|---|---|---|
| `pub async fn upload(&self, content: &[u8]) -> Result<UploadResult, ApiError>` | `POST /content/upload`, `application/octet-stream` | `:292` / `:296` |
| `pub async fn quota(&self) -> Result<Quota, ApiError>` | `GET /account/quota` | `:283` / `:285` |
| `pub async fn register(&self, names: &[NameRegistration]) -> Result<(), ApiError>` | `POST /registry/register` | `:255` / `:260` |
| `pub async fn retire(&self, targets: &[String]) -> Result<(), ApiError>` | `POST /registry/retire` | `:269` / `:274` |

Callers: `register` ← `net/publish.rs:139` (register-first, live); `retire` ← `net/retire.rs:24` (live). **`upload` and `quota` have ZERO production callers** — only `crates/contract/tests/contract.rs:419,432,452` and `:336,407,425,445,462`. The wire is proven by the contract suite; the engine simply never calls it.

`PublishRequest { name, signer, head_cid, content_cids: Vec<String>, min_current_sequence }` — `net/publish.rs:38-53`; `content_cids` is documented as "content CIDs to register/pin under this name" (`:46-47`) and flows into `NameRegistration` at `publish.rs:64-70` → `register` at `:139`. **Every production producer passes an empty vec** — `facade.rs:1162` `content_cids: Vec::new()` is the only non-test `HeldMaterial` construction (that is issue **#797**).

`Http` seam — `crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:131` `async fn send(HttpRequest) -> SeamResult<HttpResponse>`, `:152` `async fn send_capped(request, max_bytes)`. `HttpRequest.body: Option<Vec<u8>>` (`:75-82`), `HttpResponse.body: Vec<u8>` (`:100-107`). **No multipart, no streaming.** `upload` does `content.to_vec()` (`client.rs:298`) and `request_authed` clones again for the 401 retry (`client.rs:438`) — up to 3× resident for a route capped at 100 MiB server-side.

**API side (issue #629 / PR `a8220501d`)** — `POST /content/upload` at `apps/api/src/content/content.controller.ts:30`; raw-body capture gated behind a verified bearer at `apps/api/src/app-setup.ts:35-71`, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` default 100 MiB (`:8`). `content.service.ts:152` `upload()` = hash (`:162`) → pin semaphore + advisory lock (`:168-170`) → tx `registerPin` (`:176`) → post-commit `pinStore.pin` with CID-mismatch check and compensation (`:194-293`). Quota gate at `content.service.ts:210-281`: BYO → 409 (`:246-248`), idempotent short-circuit (`:256`), `sumHostedBytes`/`resolveLimitBytes`/`exceedsQuota` → **413** (`:265-269`). Tables: `pinned_cids` (`registry/entities/pinned-cid.entity.ts:35`), `name_inventory`. OpenAPI: `apps/api/openapi.json:638-690`.

### 1.6 Seams a write path would use

Six load-bearing seams (`blueprint/engine.md:69-90`): `FloorStore`, `RecordTransport`, `Http`, `Mailbox`, `RefreshHintSource`, `Scheduler`, `StagingStore`, `SnapshotCache`, `CredentialStore`. Relevant to write: **`StagingStore`** ("Durable op queue + staged upload bytes (profile-scoped budget)" — `engine.md:81`), **`Http`** (API client + gateway + BYO providers), **`RecordTransport`** (record PUT), **`FloorStore`** (sequence floors for CAS). There is **no `Provider`/`PinProvider` trait** — `content/provider.rs` is a config + prober, not a seam.

---

## 2. What is missing — "user hands us a File" → "child readable by #811's read path"

Ordered by dependency depth. Items 3–6 are *not content-specific* — they are the whole missing write plane.

1. **Facade sealing step** — `Engine::command`'s `Create` arm (`facade.rs:1244-1251`) must mint `ContentKey::generate` + call `seal_content` and pass sealed bytes to `stage_op`. An `UpdateContent` arm must be added to the catch-all (`facade.rs:1285-1287`). Both trivially available; both missing.
2. **`stage_and_notify` content variant** — `facade.rs:1581-1597` hardcodes `upload = None` and maps `RejectedOverBudget` to an internal `EngineError::Seam`. There is **no `EngineError::OverBudget` variant** (`facade.rs:449-512`), so the "uploads fail fast past the budget, metadata ops queue unbounded" law (`engine.md:233-235`) is unexpressible today.
3. **A queue-drain / publish driver.** Does not exist anywhere. Must: `queued_ops` → `decode_queue` → `replay(gate_passing, local, ops)` → per applied op author a record → publish → `remove_op` + `remove_staged_bytes` → GC orphans. Natural home beside `spawn_resolve_tick_loop` (`facade.rs:1108`).
4. **A record-authoring path.** `seal_read_body`/`encode_envelope` are **test-only in the engine** (confirmed §0). Missing: build `ReadBody::File { versions }` and `ReadBody::Folder { children }`, seal under the node's derived read key, encode the envelope, sign, and derive the child's own `ipnsName` via `SessionIdentity::write_name_signer` (`session.rs:147-152`, currently used only for the root by liveness/resolve).
5. **Head-block upload.** The record value is `/ipfs/<head_cid>`; the read path fetches blocks from a trustless gateway. Nothing uploads the envelope block, the DAG root block, or the leaf blocks. `ApiClient::upload` (`client.rs:292`) exists and is unused. Needed: upload leaves + root + envelope, collect CIDs, feed `PublishRequest.content_cids` (today always `Vec::new()`).
6. **Publish wiring for a new child name.** `net/publish.rs:115` exists (register-first → floor+1 CAS → fanout PUT → confirm-by-re-resolve) but is only called by liveness/revival. A new child needs first-publish-at-sequence-1 semantics (`core.md:207`) and the parent folder record republished with the new `ChildRef`.
7. **Parent child-ref authoring** — `{id, name, ipnsName, kind, linkCounter}` (`core.md:110-113`). No producer exists. All four #812 debts land here or in (4)/(5).
8. **Pin-provider decision.** `PinMode` (`content/provider.rs:25-32`) has zero consumers; `pre_flight_quota_check` (`retention.rs:32`) has zero callers; `ApiClient::quota` has zero engine callers.
9. **Optimistic overlay projection for content.** `overlay.rs:48-52` bumps `content_version` only; a pending upload renders with `size: None` / no mtime.
10. **Upload-side op progress.** `OpPhase` has only `Download*` (`facade.rs:438-445`) and `emit_op_progress` always sets `op_id: None` (`facade.rs:1524`). #807 requires per-file progress keyed on the upload's op id.
11. **Cancel.** `blueprint/web-client.md:193-194` requires "cancel is a facade command killing the op before publish". No such `Command` variant exists.
12. **Dead-letter population from replay.** `facade.rs:769` `dead_letters` is filled only from the undecodable sweep (`:1016`); `ReplayReport::dead_letters` never reaches it.
13. **Engine-side content KAT.** No frozen vector for an assembled DAG root; no `crates/engine/tests/` content test file.

---

## 3. Blueprint normative view (quote exactly; these are the ubiquitous-language terms)

### `blueprint/core.md`

> **:106-110** — "**Read-body**: tagged union `folder {children[]}` | `file {versions[]}` plus `createdAt`/`modifiedAt` (injected timestamps). ## 5. Open questions — the genuine forks

### Q1. Is this one slice or several? Where does the seam cut?

**Why it's a fork:** items 3–7 in §2 (queue drain, record authoring, block upload, child publish, child-ref authoring) are *not content-specific* — they are the entire missing write plane, needed equally by `mkdir`. Today `Create{content: None}` "succeeds" and publishes nothing. Framing this as "the content write slice" mis-scopes it.

Candidates: **(a)** one big slice; **(b)** split into `write-plane publish driver (metadata)` → `content sealing + upload` → `#812 guards`, where (b1) makes `mkdir` actually publish and is independently testable; **(c)** carve out a "publish a single child record" primitive first and drive both from it.

Recommendation to put to the human: **(b)**, because the metadata publish driver is provable end-to-end against #811's read path with zero content bytes, and #812's four guards attach cleanly to the record-authoring layer once it exists.

### Q2. Does the content path go through the op queue, or bypass it?

**Why it's a fork:** the blueprint is unambiguous that it goes through (`engine.md:208-211`, `CONTEXT.md:52`, `web-client.md:191-193` "one journaled op regardless of online state"), and the op model already carries `content_staging_key`. But the *sealed bytes* must be uploaded before publish, and upload requires the network. So the fork is really **when**: does the drain driver upload at drain time (offline-correct, but the content key is minted at command time and must survive in the op/staging plane), or does `Engine::command` seal-and-upload eagerly and only journal a CID?

Candidates: (a) seal at command time → stage sealed bytes → upload at drain (blueprint-aligned, requires the content key to persist across the boundary); (b) seal+upload at command time (breaks offline parity); (c) seal at command time, upload at command time when online, at drain when offline (two code paths, worst of both).

**Sub-fork with a security edge:** where does the per-version content key live between `Engine::command` and publish? It cannot be re-derived (KDF non-edge, `kdf/mod.rs:18-20`). Either it rides the `Op` (a plaintext secret in the durable op queue — the `Op` codec is serde_json, `op.rs:178-187`), or it goes into the `StagingStore` alongside the bytes, or it is held in memory (lost on crash → orphaned staged bytes, unrecoverable version). `staging.rs:40-42` currently guarantees "no plaintext user content ever lands in the staging store at rest" — a bare content key at rest is arguably worse.

### Q3. Chunk framing: engine or client?

**Why it's a fork:** `core.md:266-268` says core "ships the content-seal primitive over caller-framed chunks" and hands framing to the engine; `engine.md:483-487` confirms the engine frames. But #807/`web-client.md:189` says the UI hands a **`File` handle** (transferred), and the `Http` seam takes only `Option<Vec<u8>>` (`seams/http.rs:75-82`) with no streaming. So the whole file must materialize in the WASM worker's heap, be sealed, and then be copied again per upload.

Candidates: (a) engine frames from a full in-memory `Vec<u8>` (simplest, blows up on large files in a browser tab); (b) the client slices the `File` and feeds the engine chunk-at-a-time through a facade streaming API (contradicts "one journaled op", needs a new facade shape); (c) engine frames but the `Http` seam gains a streaming/`ReadableStream` body (a seam change; #641 is already parked on the wasm buffering issue, `seams/http.rs:143-148`).

This decision also fixes the answer to "what is the max uploadable file in v2.0" — currently bounded by RAM, and the API caps at 100 MiB (`app-setup.ts:8`).

### Q4. Upload before or after the op commits — and what is the rollback?

**Why it's a fork:** blocks must be uploaded and pinned before the record is published, or the read path gets a valid record pointing at unfetchable CIDs. But `register-first` (`CONTEXT.md:71`) says the name/CID batch registers *before* first publish. Meanwhile the API's `POST /content/upload` **already** creates the `pinned_cids` row (`content.service.ts:176-281`), and `POST /registry/register` also creates rows at `size: '0'` (`registry.service.ts:174-178`). So there are two ingress paths for a pin row and the ordering between them is not specified anywhere.

Candidates: (a) `upload(leaves) → upload(root) → upload(envelope) → register(name, contentCids) → publish`; (b) `register(name, contentCids) → upload → publish` (true register-first, but you must know the CIDs before uploading, which you do — `compute_cid` is local); (c) upload-only and let upload's own pin row satisfy inventory (skips name registration — violates register-first).

Rollback fork: if publish fails after upload, the uploaded blocks are pinned and quota-charged with no record referencing them. Is that GC'd via `retire`, left for the "registered-never-published orphan, alert-GC'd" residual (`CONTEXT.md:71`), or retried from the still-queued op?

### Q5. Which `PinMode`, and is the pre-flight quota check in or out?

**Why it's a fork:** `engine.md:474-476` says "the engine decides where bytes go" across Hosted/External/Dual, and `PinMode` is already defined (`content/provider.rs:25-32`) with zero consumers. `engine.md:469-470` explicitly marks the pre-flight quota query as **"judgment"** — i.e. an unmade decision. **Issue #705 is a landmine**: the moment `PinMode::Dual` is wired, `pre_flight_quota_check` (`retention.rs:32-45`) short-circuits on an account-level `advisory` boolean and would let hosted bytes skip the fail-fast check.

Candidates: (a) v2.0 ships Hosted only, `PinMode` stays dormant, #705 stays deferred; (b) ship Hosted + External, no Dual; (c) ship all three and fix #705 in-slice (advisory must track the byte path, not the account). Also: pre-flight quota call in (extra round trip, better UX, must handle the `sumHostedBytes`/`sumPinnedBytes` divergence) or out (rely on the authoritative 413)?

### Q6. Are chunk size and DAG shape frozen by this slice?

**Why it's a fork:** `engine.md:510-511` and `testing.md:296` say chunk size / DAG shape / retention defaults "freeze alongside the KAT manifest", and `profile.rs:36-38` calls `PRODUCTION = 1 MiB` an explicit placeholder. The DAG is currently flat/single-level (`dag.rs:12-16` names fan-out an open edge), which caps a file at ~108 GiB at 1 MiB chunks under the 4 MiB root cap (`limits.rs:12-14`). **Once a file is published with a given root shape, changing the shape is a wire-format break for already-published content.**

Candidates: (a) freeze 1 MiB + flat DAG now and add an engine-side KAT vector as part of this slice; (b) publish behind a versioned root (`chunkSize` is already in the manifest, so readers tolerate a change — but a fan-out level is *not* forward-compatible with the current `decode_root`); (c) defer the freeze and accept that pre-freeze published content may need migration.

### Q7. Does the read path re-fetch the just-written content, or does the write path seed the cache?

**Why it's a fork:** `read_content` (`facade.rs:1404-1519`) reads from the **base snapshot only** and returns `ContentUnavailable("content not yet published")` for a node with a pending op (`:1413-1427`). Right after an upload, the user immediately previews the file. Either the write path seeds `SnapshotCache`/base snapshot on publish success, or the UI eats a full resolve + gateway round trip for bytes it just held in memory.

Candidates: (a) publish success repaints the base snapshot (mirrors `project_child_version`, `sync/project.rs:50-63`) and the read goes over the network; (b) additionally cache the plaintext or sealed blocks locally; (c) do nothing and accept the latency. Note (b) reintroduces plaintext at rest, which `staging.rs:40-42` deliberately forbids.

### Q8. Cancel semantics.

**Why it's a fork:** `web-client.md:193-194` and #807 both require cancel "killing the op before publish", but no `Command` variant exists and the op queue has no cancel path (`remove_op` is only called from the undecodable sweep, `facade.rs:1024`). Candidates: (a) a new `Command::CancelOp { op_id }` — but `OpId` is a staging-store detail not exposed through the facade today; (b) cancel keyed on `NodeId`; (c) defer cancel to a follow-up and let #807 ship without it (contradicts its stated test "cancel kills the op").

### Q9. Which layer owns the #812 guards?

**Why it's a fork:** guard 3 ("`Version::new` and DAG `assemble` take `size` independently; seal/publish must tie them") can be enforced in **core** (make `Version::new` take a `SealedContent`-derived size, a core API change with KAT implications) or in the **engine** (a release-active check in `seal_content`/the publish path). Guards 1 and 4 similarly sit at either the core seal API or the engine's authoring layer. Choosing core means touching frozen encodings and the KAT manifest; choosing engine means the guarantee is per-callsite rather than structural.

### Q10. Does the drain driver share a publish port with rotation (#635)?

**Why it's a fork:** `rotation/rotate_write.rs:157-180` already defines `WriteWavePublisher` (register / is_republished / republish / retire / publish_repoint) and `grants/create.rs:51` references a `ScopeRootPublisher` — both abstract, both faked in tests, both awaiting "real wiring is #745/#746". If the content slice builds a *second*, concrete publish path over `net::publish::publish`, the codebase ends up with two publish drivers and two register-first implementations. Candidates: (a) build the concrete driver and later back the rotation traits with it; (b) implement the rotation traits first and route content publish through them; (c) let them diverge and reconcile later (a documented debt).

## 2. What is missing — "user hands us a File" → "child readable by #811's read path"

Ordered by dependency depth. Items 3–6 are *not content-specific* — they are the whole missing write plane.

1. **Facade sealing step** — `Engine::command`'s `Create` arm (`facade.rs:1244-1251`) must mint `ContentKey::generate` + call `seal_content` and pass sealed bytes to `stage_op`. An `UpdateContent` arm must be added to the catch-all (`facade.rs:1285-1287`). Both trivially available; both missing.
2. **`stage_and_notify` content variant** — `facade.rs:1581-1597` hardcodes `upload = None` and maps `RejectedOverBudget` to an internal `EngineError::Seam`. There is **no `EngineError::OverBudget` variant** (`facade.rs:449-512`), so the "uploads fail fast past the budget, metadata ops queue unbounded" law (`engine.md:233-235`) is unexpressible today.
3. **A queue-drain / publish driver.** Does not exist anywhere. Must: `queued_ops` → `decode_queue` → `replay(gate_passing, local, ops)` → per applied op author a record → publish → `remove_op` + `remove_staged_bytes` → GC orphans. Natural home beside `spawn_resolve_tick_loop` (`facade.rs:1108`).
4. **A record-authoring path.** `seal_read_body`/`encode_envelope` are **test-only in the engine** (confirmed §0). Missing: build `ReadBody::File { versions }` and `ReadBody::Folder { children }`, seal under the node's derived read key, encode the envelope, sign, and derive the child's own `ipnsName` via `SessionIdentity::write_name_signer` (`session.rs:147-152`, currently used only for the root by liveness/resolve).
5. **Head-block upload.** The record value is `/ipfs/<head_cid>`; the read path fetches blocks from a trustless gateway. Nothing uploads the envelope block, the DAG root block, or the leaf blocks. `ApiClient::upload` (`client.rs:292`) exists and is unused. Needed: upload leaves + root + envelope, collect CIDs, feed `PublishRequest.content_cids` (today always `Vec::new()`).
6. **Publish wiring for a new child name.** `net/publish.rs:115` exists (register-first → floor+1 CAS → fanout PUT → confirm-by-re-resolve) but is only called by liveness/revival. A new child needs first-publish-at-sequence-1 semantics (`core.md:207`) and the parent folder record republished with the new `ChildRef`.
7. **Parent child-ref authoring** — `{id, name, ipnsName, kind, linkCounter}` (`core.md:110-113`). No producer exists. All four #812 debts land here or in (4)/(5).
8. **Pin-provider decision.** `PinMode` (`content/provider.rs:25-32`) has zero consumers; `pre_flight_quota_check` (`retention.rs:32`) has zero callers; `ApiClient::quota` has zero engine callers.
9. **Optimistic overlay projection for content.** `overlay.rs:48-52` bumps `content_version` only; a pending upload renders with `size: None` / no mtime.
10. **Upload-side op progress.** `OpPhase` has only `Download*` (`facade.rs:438-445`) and `emit_op_progress` always sets `op_id: None` (`facade.rs:1524`). #807 requires per-file progress keyed on the upload's op id.
11. **Cancel.** `blueprint/web-client.md:193-194` requires "cancel is a facade command killing the op before publish". No such `Command` variant exists.
12. **Dead-letter population from replay.** `facade.rs:769` `dead_letters` is filled only from the undecodable sweep (`:1016`); `ReplayReport::dead_letters` never reaches it.
13. **Engine-side content KAT.** No frozen vector for an assembled DAG root; no `crates/engine/tests/` content test file.

### Issue #812 — encode-side fail-closed guards (OPEN, explicitly blocked on this slice)

Title: *engine/core: encode-side fail-closed guards for the child read-path rejects*. Body states: "Depends on the engine content-bearing write / upload slice (surfaces via #807)". Four debts, each needing a **release-active `Err`** (never `debug_assert!`) plus a release-firing test:

4. **Child-ref `ipnsName` well-formedness** — the read path parses canonical base36 fail-closed (`facade.rs:1434-1441`); authoring must emit exactly that form.

Precedent cited: #794 (still open — `core: encode-side recursion depth bound is debug_assert-only, unbounded in release`).
